title: Self-Similar

language.notes: Narrator stays clean, neutral English. Optional code-switching flavor: NPCs and environmental text (signage, PA announcements, old memos) may carry lines in Spanish, French, Italian, or Portuguese per that character's background — left partly untranslated for atmosphere, never load-bearing for solving anything. Draws on a generic North American corporate-tower palette plus whatever a given echo/NPC's backstory implies.

learning.concept: Fractal geometry & iterated function systems: self-similarity, fractal dimension, attractors, and the fixed point of a recursive map -- applied literally to a building generated by recursion, and metaphorically to a life generated by repeated choices

theme: A 35-year-old man alone in an empty corporate tower on a late shift discovers the building is recursing on itself -- a liminal horror built on real fractal mathematics, doubling as his own existential reckoning with a life that keeps repeating its own pattern
